routes.label: Add the square and triangle areas

question:
Equilateral \(\triangle ABC\) has side length \(1,\) and squares \(ABDE,\) \(BCHI,\) \(CAFG\) lie outside the triangle. What is the area of hexagon \(DEFGHI?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_10A_Q13_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The drawn square edges partition the hexagon into three unit squares, the central triangle \(ABC\), and the three gap triangles \(AEF\), \(BDI\), and \(CGH\). These pieces fill the hexagon without overlapping interiors.

At \(A\), the two square angles and the equilateral triangle's angle leave
\[
\angle EAF=360^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ=120^\circ.
\]
The same calculation applies at \(B\) and \(C\). Thus each gap triangle has two sides of length \(1\) enclosing a \(120^\circ\) angle.

Draw the altitude from the \(120^\circ\) vertex of one gap triangle. Since the triangle is isosceles, this altitude bisects both the vertex angle and the opposite side. It creates two right triangles with angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\), each with hypotenuse \(1\). The altitude is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, so its length is \(1/2\). By the Pythagorean theorem, half the base is
\[
\sqrt{1-\left(\frac12\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Each gap triangle therefore has area
\[
\frac12\cdot\sqrt3\cdot\frac12=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}.
\]
The altitude of the central equilateral triangle also bisects its unit base. Its height is \(\sqrt3/2\), so its area is \(\sqrt3/4\).

Adding all seven pieces gives
\[
[DEFGHI]=3\cdot1^2+4\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}=3+\sqrt3.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{3+\sqrt3}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
